title: Eligibility-Period Settings of the Patient Hardship Discount Program: Income Changes, Revocation and Insurance Recovery
content:
While a Patient Hardship Discount Program determination is in its eligibility period, four settings per level govern income changes, revocation and later insurance payments.

| Level | Calendar days to report a household income change during the eligibility period | A reported income change triggers a new level determination | Calendar days back from a revocation over which discounts are reversed | Discount reversed when insurance later pays the discounted charge |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hardship Discount Level 1 (25%) | 30 | Yes | 365 | Yes |
| Hardship Discount Level 2 (50%) | 30 | Yes | 365 | Yes |
| Hardship Discount Level 3 (75%) | 30 | Yes | 365 | Yes |
| Hardship Discount Level 4 (100%) | 30 | Yes | 365 | Yes |
| Catastrophic Medical Hardship | 30 | Yes | 365 | Yes |
| Presumptive Eligibility Discount | 30 | No | 365 | Yes |

### Settings explained

- **Reporting period.** The patient must report a household income change during the eligibility period within the number of calendar days shown — 30 at every level.
- **New level determination.** Whether a reported income change triggers a new level determination. It does at every income-tested level and does not at the Presumptive Eligibility Discount.
- **Revocation look-back.** The number of calendar days back from a revocation over which discounts granted under the revoked determination are reversed — 365 at every level.
- **Insurance recovery.** Whether a discount is reversed when insurance later pays the discounted charge — yes at every level.

### Example reading (hypothetical)

A patient at Hardship Discount Level 2 (50%) whose household income changes reports it within 30 calendar days, and the change triggers a new level determination. A patient at the Presumptive Eligibility Discount has the same 30 days to report, but the report triggers no new level determination at that level.
